message.content: **Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and decided to buy. The fundamentals support a modest long position: total net sales of $391.0B (up 2% from $383.3B), operating income of $123.2B, net income of $93.7B, diluted EPS of $6.08, and operating cash flow of $118.3B — with gross margin expanding to 46.2% (from 44.1%) on Services strength ($96.2B, +13%, at 73.9% services gross margin), $140.8B of unrestricted cash and marketable securities, and $95.0B returned via buybacks plus $15.2B of dividends. The main blemishes are the $10.2B one-time State Aid tax charge (which pushed the effective tax rate to 24.1% and net income down 3.4% year over year), an 8% decline in Greater China sales, and flat iPhone revenue — none of which I view as impairing the franchise. With AAPL quoted at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), I placed a single buy limit order for 40 shares at $223.00, which filled at $223.00 for a total of $8,920 — inside the $10,000 per-order cap, well under the $20,000 daily cap, and funded entirely from the account's $50,000 cash with no money moved out.
message.reasoning:
